selected.prompt: Points A, B and C have position vectors (1,2), (7,−1) and (−2,8). P is the midpoint of BC and Q is the midpoint of AC. (a) Find the position vectors of P and Q. (b) Show by vector methods that the points on AP and BQ two-thirds of the way from A and B respectively coincide. (c) Give their common position vector and the ratio AG:GP. [8 marks]
selected.modelAnswer: P=(5/2,7/2), Q=(−1/2,5). AP=(3/2,3/2), so A+(2/3)AP=(1,2)+(1,1)=(2,3). BQ=(−15/2,6), so B+(2/3)BQ=(7,−1)+(−5,4)=(2,3). Both medians contain G=(2,3), two-thirds from their vertex. Thus they intersect at G, and AG:GP=(2/3):(1/3)=2:1.
markPoints: Point G on AP at 2/3 has G=A+(2/3)AP=(2,3).
Point H on BQ at 2/3 has H=B+(2/3)BQ=(2,3).
Since G=H, the medians AP and BQ meet at the common point with position vector (2,3).
AG:GP=2:1 because G lies 2/3 of the way from A to P.

selected.prompt: A circle is given by x²+y²−4x−6y−12=0. (a) Find its centre and radius. (b) Verify that P=(5,7) lies on the circle. (c) Find an exact equation of the tangent to the circle at P. (d) Find both axis intercepts of this tangent. [7 marks]
selected.modelAnswer: Complete squares: (x−2)²+(y−3)²=25, so centre (2,3) and radius 5. At P=(5,7), CP=(3,4) and |CP|=5, so P lies on the circle. Radius slope=4/3; tangent slope=−3/4. Through P: y−7=−(3/4)(x−5), hence 3x+4y=43. The x- and y-intercepts are (43/3,0) and (0,43/4).
markPoints: For P=(5,7), displacement from centre is (3,4), whose squared length is 3²+4²=25.
Tangent is perpendicular to CP and has gradient −3/4.

selected.prompt: Let f(x)=x²−4x+1 and g(x)=−2f(1−2x)+3. (a) Complete the square for f. (b) Describe a valid ordered sequence of graph transformations giving y=g(x) from y=f(x). (c) Express g as a quadratic in x and find the turning point. (d) Find both exact x-intercepts of g. [9 marks]
selected.modelAnswer: f(x)=(x−2)²−3. One valid sequence is reflect in the y-axis, horizontally compress by scale factor 1/2, then translate right by 1/2; reflect in the x-axis, stretch vertically by factor 2, then translate up by 3. Algebra: f(1−2x)=(1−2x)²−4(1−2x)+1=4x²+4x−2, so g=−8x²−8x+7=−8(x+1/2)²+9. Turning point (−1/2,9). Setting g=0 gives 8x²+8x−7=0, so x=(−2±3√2)/4. Equivalent orders of compatible transformations earn credit.
markPoints: Horizontal reflection in the y-axis is part of one valid transformation sequence.
Horizontal compression by scale factor 1/2, applied to the reflected graph.
Translation right by 1/2, giving f(1−2x) from f(x); alternative valid composite transformations are creditable.
Vertical reflection in the x-axis and stretch by factor 2, giving −2f(1−2x).
Writes g(x)=−8(x+1/2)²+9 and identifies turning point (−1/2,9).
Solves g=0 to give exact roots x=(−2+3√2)/4 and x=(−2−3√2)/4.

selected.prompt: In the expansion of (1+ax)⁷, the coefficient of x² is 84 and the coefficient of x³ is negative. (a) Show that a²=4. (b) Find a. (c) Calculate the coefficients of x³ and x⁴, showing the binomial coefficients used. [7 marks]
selected.modelAnswer: The x² coefficient is C(7,2)a²=21a². Hence 21a²=84, so a²=4 and a=±2. The x³ coefficient is C(7,3)a³=35a³, which is negative only for a=−2. Then x³ coefficient=35(−8)=−280; x⁴ coefficient=C(7,4)(−2)⁴=35×16=560.
markPoints: Uses the x² term C(7,2)a²x² and evaluates C(7,2)=21.
Obtains a²=4 and the candidates a=±2.
Uses the negative x³ coefficient, C(7,3)a³, to choose a=−2.

selected.prompt: For y=x²−5x+6 over 0≤x≤4, calculate (a) the signed definite integral from 0 to 4 and (b) the total area between the curve and the x-axis. You must show where the graph lies below the axis and split the integral correctly. Give exact answers. [8 marks]
selected.modelAnswer: y=(x−2)(x−3), with roots 2 and 3. The curve is above the x-axis on [0,2] and [3,4], and below on (2,3). F(x)=x³/3−5x²/2+6x. F(0)=0, F(2)=14/3, F(3)=9/2 and F(4)=16/3. Signed integral=16/3. Total area=[F(2)−F(0)]−[F(3)−F(2)]+[F(4)−F(3)]=14/3+1/6+5/6=17/3.
markPoints: Factorises y=(x−2)(x−3) and finds zeros x=2,3.
Correctly identifies y<0 only on 2<x<3 over the stated domain.
Writes total area ∫₀²y dx − ∫₂³y dx + ∫₃⁴y dx, reversing the negative strip.
